title: Strong Goldbach: The Minimal Symmetric Offset (Innermost Partition)
description: A fully verified, axiom-free study of the MINIMAL symmetric offset for the Strong/Binary Goldbach reformulation — the offset k of the innermost Goldbach partition (m−k, m+k) of 2m, whose two primes sit closest to the midpoint m. This complements the parent entry, which bounds the NUMBER of Goldbach partitions (the comet count); here the object is WHERE the first one sits. Defines minimalSymmetricOffset via Nat.find on the parent's decidable symmetric-pair predicate (with an out-of-range sentinel m when 2m has no partition), and proves: (1) it is a genuine symmetric offset and the least one (minimalSymmetricOffset_le); (2) it is in range (< m) iff a Goldbach partition exists, tied to the parent's comet count being positive; (3) the diagonal law minimalSymmetricOffset m = 0 ↔ m prime — the innermost partition is the diagonal 2m = m+m exactly at prime midpoints; (4) the prime-gap connection: the larger summand m + off is the SMALLEST prime j ≥ m whose reflection 2m−j is also prime, and dually the smaller summand is the GREATEST prime ≤ m with prime complement (add_minimalSymmetricOffset_le / le_sub_minimalSymmetricOffset), so a large minimal offset encodes a run of primes near m all of whose Goldbach complements are composite; (5) inherited structure — at composite m the offset is a nonzero totative of m and, for m > 2, of opposite parity to m; and (6) a NEW reformulation of Strong Goldbach: the conjecture is EQUIVALENT to the minimal offset being well-defined (< m) for every m ≥ 2 (symmetricGoldbach_iff_minimalSymmetricOffset_lt), the minimal-offset analogue of the parent's comet-positivity form. Concrete minimal offsets verified by kernel `decide` (0=prime midpoint 5; 1 at 4,6; 2 at 9; 3 at 34). The Strong Goldbach Conjecture itself is NOT proved — a general upper bound on the minimal offset is equivalent to the conjecture and remains open. 17 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. The file is axiom-free: `#print axioms` on the headline results (symmetricGoldbach_iff_minimalSymmetricOffset_lt, add_minimalSymmetricOffset_le, minimalSymmetricOffset_eq_zero_iff) shows only the ordinary foundational axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound — no `sorryAx`, no `Lean.ofReduceBool`. All concrete values use kernel `decide` (pinned via Nat.find_eq_iff so only small primality facts are reduced), not `native_decide`. This file does NOT prove the Strong Goldbach Conjecture, which remains open; it studies the minimal-offset object and proves an equivalent reformulation of the conjecture in terms of it.
originalContributions: minimalSymmetricOffset: the least offset k with m−k and m+k both prime — the innermost Goldbach partition of 2m — defined by Nat.find on the parent's decidable symmetric-pair predicate, with the out-of-range sentinel m marking the no-partition case
minimalSymmetricOffset_le: minimality — every symmetric offset (both m−k, m+k prime) is at least the minimal one

minimalSymmetricOffset_lt_iff / minimalSymmetricOffset_lt_iff_count_pos: the minimal offset is in range (< m) iff 2m has a Goldbach partition iff the parent's comet count symmetricPairCount m is positive — the sentinel makes `< m` a clean existence test

minimalSymmetricOffset_eq_zero_iff: the diagonal law — when a partition exists, the innermost offset is 0 exactly when the midpoint m is prime (the trivial pair 2m = m+m); minimalSymmetricOffset_eq_zero_of_prime gives the unconditional forward direction
add_minimalSymmetricOffset_le: prime-gap connection — the larger summand m + minimalSymmetricOffset m is the SMALLEST prime j ≥ m whose reflection 2m−j is also prime

le_sub_minimalSymmetricOffset: dual — the smaller summand m − minimalSymmetricOffset m is the GREATEST prime p ≤ m whose complement 2m−p is also prime; together these say a large minimal offset means a run of primes near m all with composite Goldbach complement
minimalSymmetricOffset_coprime_of_not_prime: at composite m the minimal offset is a nonzero totative of m (coprime), by specializing the parent's symmetric_pair_offset_coprime to the innermost pair
minimalSymmetricOffset_parity: for m > 2 the minimal offset has opposite parity to m (both summands odd), specializing the parent's symmetric_pair_offset_parity

symmetricGoldbach_iff_minimalSymmetricOffset_lt: a new reformulation — the Symmetric (hence Strong) Goldbach Conjecture is equivalent to the minimal offset being well-defined (< m) for every m ≥ 2; the minimal-offset analogue of the parent's symmetricGoldbach_iff_count
minimalSymmetricOffset_lt_of_symmetricGoldbach: under the conjecture, the minimal offset is in range at every m ≥ 2
prime_sub_minimalSymmetricOffset / prime_add_minimalSymmetricOffset: the summands at the minimal offset are prime
minimalSymmetricOffset_pos_of_not_prime: at composite midpoints the innermost partition is genuinely off-diagonal (offset > 0)

crossReferences.description: Parent entry: the symmetric-prime-pair reformulation of Strong Goldbach and the comet counting function symmetricPairCount with its upper bounds (parity, single-prime sieve, Euler-totient). This follow-up imports that file and studies the complementary minimal-offset object — where the innermost partition sits rather than how many partitions exist — reusing the parent's decidable instance, coprimality (symmetric_pair_offset_coprime) and parity (symmetric_pair_offset_parity) lemmas, and comet count.
The Weak (Ternary) Goldbach entry defines IsSumOfTwoPrimes and the Binary Goldbach statement reformulated here; the minimal offset gives a further equivalent form of that same conjecture.

overview.historicalContext: In his 1742 letter to Euler, Goldbach conjectured that every even integer greater than 2 is a sum of two primes — the Strong (Binary) Goldbach Conjecture, still open after nearly three centuries despite verification past 4·10^18. Writing an even number as 2m, each representation 2m = (m−k) + (m+k) is symmetric about the midpoint m, so a Goldbach partition is a symmetric offset k with both m−k and m+k prime. The classical picture of the conjecture is the Goldbach comet — the plot of the number of such partitions against 2m, always positive and growing. The parent entry formalizes that count (symmetricPairCount). This entry turns to the complementary extremal object: not how many partitions exist, but where the closest one to the midpoint sits.
overview.problemStatement: For each m, among all offsets k with 2m = (m−k) + (m+k) and both summands prime, study the minimal such k — the innermost Goldbach partition of 2m. Define minimalSymmetricOffset m as the least symmetric offset (via Nat.find on the parent's decidable symmetric-pair predicate), with an out-of-range sentinel value m when 2m has no partition. Characterize it (minimality, in-range ⟺ existence), locate its diagonal (offset 0 ⟺ m prime), connect it to prime gaps (its summands are the extreme Goldbach primes bracketing m), inherit the parent's coprimality/parity structure, and express the Strong Goldbach Conjecture as an equivalent statement about it.
overview.proofStrategy: Six moves. (1) Define minimalSymmetricOffset m by Nat.find on the parent's decidable predicate "m−k and m+k are both prime", using the sentinel m for the no-partition case so that `< m` is a decidable in-range test. (2) Extract minimality from Nat.find_min' and the summands' primality / sum-to-2m from the found witness. (3) Prove minimalSymmetricOffset m < m ⟺ a Goldbach partition exists ⟺ symmetricPairCount m > 0, tying the sentinel to the parent's comet count. (4) The diagonal law: when a partition exists, the offset is 0 exactly at prime midpoints (the trivial pair 2m = m+m), and strictly positive at composite midpoints. (5) The prime-gap connection: m + offset is the smallest prime ≥ m whose reflection 2m−j is prime, and m − offset the greatest prime ≤ m with prime complement — so a large minimal offset is a run of primes near m all of whose Goldbach complements are composite. (6) Specialize the parent's coprimality and parity lemmas to the innermost pair, and package the whole thing as the reformulation symmetricGoldbach_iff_minimalSymmetricOffset_lt. Concrete offsets (0 at 5, 1 at 4 and 6, 2 at 9, 3 at 34) are pinned by kernel `decide` via Nat.find_eq_iff, keeping the proof axiom-free (no native_decide).
keyInsights: The minimal offset is the extremal "where" companion to the parent comet's "how many": it names the single innermost Goldbach partition of 2m, the one whose two primes sit closest to the midpoint m.

The out-of-range sentinel (returning m itself when 2m has no partition) is what makes the object total and decidable: `minimalSymmetricOffset m < m` is a clean existence test, provably equivalent to the parent comet count symmetricPairCount m being positive.

The diagonal law minimalSymmetricOffset m = 0 ⟺ m prime pins the offset's zero locus exactly to the trivial diagonal partition 2m = m + m; composite midpoints force a genuinely off-diagonal innermost pair (offset > 0).

The offset is a prime-gap invariant: its two summands m ± offset are the extreme Goldbach primes bracketing m, so a large minimal offset certifies a stretch of primes near m each of whose reflections across m is composite — an obstruction structurally close to large prime gaps.

Structure is inherited for free from the parent: at composite m the minimal offset is a nonzero totative of m (coprime), and for m > 2 it has opposite parity to m (both summands odd), by specializing the parent's symmetric_pair_offset_coprime / _parity to the innermost pair.

The whole study yields a new equivalent form of the conjecture — Strong Goldbach ⟺ the minimal offset is well-defined (< m) for every m ≥ 2 — the minimal-offset analogue of the parent's comet-positivity reformulation, all axiom-free with concrete values by kernel `decide`.

conclusion.summary: This entry gives a fully verified, axiom-free study of the minimal symmetric offset — the offset of the innermost Goldbach partition (m−k, m+k) of 2m. It defines minimalSymmetricOffset via Nat.find with an out-of-range sentinel, proves minimality and the in-range ⟺ existence ⟺ positive-comet-count chain, establishes the diagonal law (offset 0 ⟺ prime midpoint), the prime-gap connection (the summands are the extreme Goldbach primes bracketing m), the inherited coprimality/parity structure at composite midpoints, and a new reformulation of Strong Goldbach as the well-definedness of the minimal offset for every m ≥ 2. The Strong Goldbach Conjecture itself is not proved; a general upper bound on the minimal offset is shown to be equivalent to it. 17 theorems, 1 definition, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Recasting Goldbach through its innermost partition connects the conjecture to prime-gap phenomena: because m + offset is the smallest prime ≥ m with prime reflection, any uniform bound minimalSymmetricOffset m < f(m) with f(m) ≤ m for all m ≥ 2 would prove Strong Goldbach, so the conjecture is precisely the statement that the innermost Goldbach prime never escapes the midpoint. The offset thus packages Goldbach into a single scalar extremal quantity per even number — one whose typical smallness (offsets 0–3 already at small m) is heuristically expected but whose worst-case growth is exactly the open problem. It also supplies covering-number-free, decidable existence tests that downstream comet and prime-gap formalizations can consume.
openQuestions: A general upper bound on minimalSymmetricOffset m (e.g. minimalSymmetricOffset m < m, or a polylogarithmic bound o(m)) for all m ≥ 2 — this is equivalent to the Strong Goldbach Conjecture and remains open.

The typical and average growth of the minimal offset as m → ∞: heuristically the innermost partition sits very close to the midpoint (offset O(log^2 m) on average by Hardy–Littlewood-type reasoning), but no unconditional bound is known.

The precise relationship between large minimal offsets and large prime gaps near m: a large minimal offset certifies a run of primes near m with composite Goldbach complements — how does its extremal behavior compare to maximal prime gaps?

Whether the minimal offset attains arbitrarily large values infinitely often, and if so, the distribution of the m at which record offsets occur (the minimal-offset analogue of the Goldbach comet's lower envelope).
